matching.metric: Positive reduction = 1 - output RMSE / noisy-input RMSE against clean truth in fixed flat ROI; per-control linear luminance or two-channel opponent chroma. Same positive sign, minimum target, tolerance relative to reduction; freeze tuning before independent noise-seed acceptance.

primary.rule: Equal scene/amount weights per control. Both informative input-ground-truth detail/edge errors improve >=10%; below-floor baseline must remain below floor. Per-case regression <=max(absolute guard, relative guard*baseline). Missing support/matching or no informative target blocks acceptance.

contracts.zeroIdentity: Control zero preserves canonical noisy input hash exactly, including signed RGB; hidden RGB canonical zero. Finite output required.

scaling.rule: Independent scaling factor on the same frozen Lightcraft formula/amount: nativePixels vs unscaled. Each control mean distance to area-downsampled native output improves >=10%, all rows stay <=.002 linear opponent/luminance units. Candidate residual reduction agrees with downsampled native reduction; quality guards relative to downsampled native against correctly area-averaged clean truth. Glowroom is a separate diagnostic, not a donor of matching or Go. These guards are engineering limits, not empirical perceptual thresholds.

requiredMissingUntilMeasured: Licensed real dark/bright RAW-developed photo rasters and source-regression originals (#1129/#815)
Production process/version, explicit source/native geometry and decoder resampling provenance, cache/undo/cancellation and preview/export integration
Accelerated path parity if an integrated CI/Metal candidate is proposed
decisionOrder: Verified independent contracts, matched critical/performance failure or complete informative primary failure yields no-go per control.
Missing data/support/matching and real/visual/integration evidence block Go; no informative primary signal is blocked, never a false no-go.
Scaling has its own complete native/preview matrix and gates; no acceptance inherited from either formula.
